claim: Vol 9 governs travel and transportation entitlements
quote: Any conflict between this publication and the Joint Travel Regulations (JTR) is resolved based on the JTR and not this publication.
fix: Vol 9 supplements the JTR. The JTR controls on conflict. State the rule on every Vol 9 page.

claim: Voucher within 5 business days of return per MCO 4650.39A Ch 1 para 5.a.(2)(d)
quote: The traveler must submit all claims within five working days of return to or arrival at the PDS.
fix: Rule is five working days of return to or arrival at the PDS, from Vol 9 Ch 8 para 6.1 and MARADMIN 359/25 para 3.b. MCO 4650.39A holds no five-day paragraph. MARADMIN 359/25 does not cancel MCO 4650.39A.

claim: Travel advance supports up-front travel costs
quote: travel advances must not be authorized unless an exemption to GTCC use is granted in accordance with the GTCC Regulations
fix: Advances need a GTCC exemption and are paid by EFT, up to 80 percent of estimated allowances, 100 percent on hardship. Marine Corps recoups an unclaimed advance 15 days after estimated return, para 4.5.2.1.

claim: Premium class request needs a Constructed Travel Worksheet
quote: The cost comparison is submitted on a worksheet such as the DTMO's constructed travel worksheet (CTW) or similar locally-approved form.
fix: CTW supports a POV advantageous-to-Government comparison. It is not the premium-class support document. Premium class follows Vol 9 Ch 4 para 4.0.

claim: Constructed travel caps reimbursement at the authorized mode cost
quote: Reimbursement must be limited to the constructed cost of the authorized transportation mode

claim: Receipts attach for lodging and expenses of $75 or more
quote: The traveler must attach all lodging receipts regardless of amount and any other receipts for expenses of $75 or more to the claim.

claim: Split disbursement per DoD DTS Regulations section 030604
fix: DTS Regulations are not in the archive. MCO 4600.40C ch 2 para 5.c-d carries the split rule.

claim: Order type (TDY, PCS, evacuation) selects the Vol 9 chapter
quote: The policies addressed in Volume 9 apply to all personnel traveling under orders funded by the DoD.

claim: Evacuation allowances cover authorized evacuees including Service members
quote: Uniformed members are not evacuated; however, they may be issued orders for temporary duty (TDY) travel as required.
fix: Evacuation allowances cover dependents and civilian employees and their families. A Service member goes on TDY orders instead. Rewrite who is an evacuee.

claim: JTR Chapter 7 is the evacuation entitlement chapter
quote: CHAPTER 6: EVACUATION TRAVEL
fix: The JTR has Chapters 1 to 6. Evacuation is Chapter 6, sections 0601 to 0603. No Chapter 7 exists. Fix every cite on the page.

claim: Evacuation claim cut in DTS on DD Form 1351-2 through the standard voucher
quote: The Defense Travel System does not support evacuation travel.
fix: DTS does not process evacuation travel. Departure orders support advances and payments through the finance office, ATM or EFT.

claim: Subsistence Expense (SE) covers food and lodging at the safe haven
quote: 060205. Allowances While at the Safe Haven
fix: JTR names the allowance Allowances While at the Safe Haven, 060205, and while at the designated place, 060206. No Subsistence Expense, SE, term found.

claim: Evacuation categories: natural disaster, hostile action, ordered departure, voluntary departure
quote: 0601 EVACUATION AUTHORITY
fix: JTR frames evacuations as authorized or ordered and names the announcing official in Tables 6-1 to 6-12. The four-category list is not in Vol 9 Ch 7.

claim: State Department coordinates civilian evacuee actions
quote: the Department of State Standardized Regulations (DSSR)  600

claim: PCS voucher due within 5 business days from arrival per MCO 4650.39A
quote: The traveler must submit all claims within five working days of return to or arrival at the PDS.
fix: Rule is five working days of return to or arrival at the PDS, from Vol 9 Ch 8 para 6.1 and MARADMIN 359/25 para 3.b. MCO 4650.39A holds no five-day paragraph. MARADMIN 359/25 does not cancel MCO 4650.39A.

claim: DLA is paid by grade and dependent status per JTR Chapter 5
quote: DLA is paid to members as specified in the JTR, section 0505.

claim: Request Advance Pay on PCS under Vol 7A Ch 32
quote: DLA advance payments may be issued 30 days prior to travel rather than 10 days prior to travel as directed for most other travel advances
fix: PCS travel advances sit under Vol 9 Ch 5. DLA advance issues 30 days before travel. Vol 7A Ch 32 is advance pay of base pay.

claim: TLE applies CONUS, TLA applies OCONUS
quote: TLE for either 7 or 21 days
fix: TLE is the CONUS PCS lodging reimbursement. TLA also pays when departing an OCONUS station, not only at the gaining station.

claim: MALT pays POV mileage between duty stations per JTR Chapter 5
quote: TRANSPORTATION AND STORAGE OF POV
fix: MALT rate sits in JTR Chapter 5. Vol 9 Ch 6 does not restate it.

claim: Traveler signs within 5 business days per MCO 4650.39A Ch 1 para 5.a.(2)(d)
quote: The traveler must submit all claims within five working days of return to or arrival at the PDS.
fix: Rule is five working days of return to or arrival at the PDS, from Vol 9 Ch 8 para 6.1 and MARADMIN 359/25 para 3.b. MCO 4650.39A holds no five-day paragraph. MARADMIN 359/25 does not cancel MCO 4650.39A. Extended TDY over 45 days needs a claim for each 30-day period, filed within five working days after each period. The page omits that.

claim: Voucher routes to Disbursing within 3 business days of traveler signature per MCO 4650.39A para 5.b.2
quote: The supervisor/approving official or the travel computation office has seven calendar days to notify the traveler if the travel claim is not proper or complete
fix: No three business day routing rule found in MCO 4650.39A. Vol 9 Ch 8 gives 7 calendar days to return a defective claim and payment within 30 calendar days of receipt.

claim: Flat rate per diem cases do not require lodging receipts
quote: The traveler must attach all lodging receipts regardless of amount and any other receipts for expenses of $75 or more to the claim.
fix: No flat rate per diem exists in the JTR. Lodging receipts attach regardless of amount.

claim: Receipts for lodging and for expenses of $75 or more
quote: The traveler must attach all lodging receipts regardless of amount and any other receipts for expenses of $75 or more to the claim.

claim: AO is pecuniarily liable for improper certification
quote: Approval of this type of claim will subject Approving Officials, Authorizing Officials, and Certifying Officers to potential pecuniary liability
fix: Liability attaches to defined failures such as approving claims for other personnel. It is not automatic. Soften.

claim: Over-payment collected through DMM per MCO 4650.39A Ch 9
quote: the traveler is required to pay the indebtedness within 30 calendar days after the date of notification
fix: Collection runs under Vol 16 Ch 2 after 30 days.

claim: AO certifies per DoD DTS Regulations 030401.C and Vol 5 Ch 5
fix: DTS Regulations are not in the archive.

claim: Flat rate per diem applies to TDY greater than 30 days at a single location
quote: Long-term TDY means continuous travel for 31 days or more (other than deployment).
fix: The JTR has no flat rate per diem for Service members. Long-term TDY is a 31 day marker with its own computation rules. Wave 1 flagged the same tiers on tdy-per-diem and long-term-tdy. A pay clerk applying a flat rate would misstate per diem.

claim: Voucher within 5 business days of return per MCO 4650.39A
quote: The traveler must submit all claims within five working days of return to or arrival at the PDS.
fix: Rule is five working days of return to or arrival at the PDS, from Vol 9 Ch 8 para 6.1 and MARADMIN 359/25 para 3.b. MCO 4650.39A holds no five-day paragraph. MARADMIN 359/25 does not cancel MCO 4650.39A. TDY over 30 days files every 30 days, Vol 9 Ch 5 para 4.5.1.

claim: Process travel advance per Vol 9 Ch 5 and Vol 7A Ch 32
quote: Most travel advances should not exceed 80 percent of the estimated travel and transportation allowances.
fix: Advances need a GTCC exemption. Most are capped at 80 percent, 100 percent for hardship, and per diem advances cover at most 45 days. Vol 7A Ch 32 is not the travel advance authority.

claim: Advance aligns with expected costs up to the chapter cap
quote: Most travel advances should not exceed 80 percent of the estimated travel and transportation allowances.
fix: Name the cap - 80 percent, up to 100 percent on hardship.

claim: Marine Corps official lodging bookable in DTS effective 25 May 2026, destination set to installation, mandatory use for military and civilian
quote: Marine Corps official lodging facilities will be bookable when creating Temporary Additional Duty (TDY) authorizations in the Defense Travel System (DTS) effective 25 May 2026.

claim: Off-base lodging without certificate of non-availability caps reimbursement at official lodging rate
quote: reimbursement for lodging costs when conducting official travel will be limited to the official lodging rate when lodging is available but not utilized

claim: Receipts for lodging and expenses of $75 or more
quote: The traveler must attach all lodging receipts regardless of amount

claim: Advance liquidates on the voucher
quote: a corresponding travel claim is filed within 5 working days of the traveler's return to or arrival at the permanent duty station
fix: Marine Corps recoups an unclaimed advance 15 days after the estimated return date.

claim: Premium class requires a Constructed Travel Worksheet
quote: The cost comparison is submitted on a worksheet such as the DTMO's constructed travel worksheet (CTW) or similar locally-approved form.
fix: CTW is the POV versus common carrier comparison. First and business class follow Vol 9 Ch 4 para 4.0 and JTR Table 2-5 approvals.

claim: Constructed travel caps reimbursement at what the authorized mode would have cost
quote: Reimbursement must be limited to the constructed cost of the authorized transportation mode, which is the sum of per diem and the transportation cost

claim: Authorized route is the most direct usually-traveled route
fix: Phrase not found in cached Ch 4. JTR 020204 governs distance determinations.

claim: JTR Chapter 2 holds the transportation allowances
quote: CHAPTER 2: STANDARD TRAVEL AND TRANSPORTATION ALLOWANCES

claim: Rental car authorization flows from the AO
quote: 020209. Rental Vehicle

claim: Exception requests route through MARFOR and HQMC
quote: The Office of the Under Secretary of Defense (Comptroller) (OUSD(C)) is the approving authority for exceptions to policy.
fix: OUSD Comptroller approves Vol 9 exceptions. Requests need a DoD Component command channel recommendation at or above DCFO level and go to DFAS-ZPT. MARFOR and HQMC routing is the Component step only.

claim: Vol 9 Ch 1 governs allowances for Service members, civilians and dependents
quote: Volume 9 provides supplemental instructions on the payment of allowances authorized by the Joint Travel Regulations (JTR).
fix: Vol 9 supplements the JTR. JTR prevails on conflict.

claim: Statutory base is 5 U.S.C. and 37 U.S.C.
quote: The JTR directly implements the travel and transportation allowances authorized by law for members of the Uniformed Services
fix: Ch 1 names no title of the U.S. Code. Cite the JTR or Ch 5, 37 U.S.C. 452, 5 U.S.C. 5705 and 5724.

claim: Each chapter carries a revision date footer, maintain a chapter index
quote: *June 2025
fix: Each chapter carries its own date - Ch 1 Jun 2025, Ch 4 Aug 2024, Ch 5 Jan 2026, Ch 6 May 2025, Ch 7 Feb 2025, Ch 8 Apr 2024.

claim: Voucher approved but no payment posted within 7 days is a dispute scenario
quote: The disbursing office pays the travel claim within 30 calendar days after the claim is signed and dated as received by the supervisor/approving official.
fix: Payment standard is 30 calendar days from receipt, with a late payment fee after that. Seven days is early. Late-payment fees apply from day 31.

claim: DFAS adjusts split disbursement, paid voucher amounts and GTCC routing errors
fix: No archive source for dispute routing. Cite the DFAS or FPM Vol 2 procedure.

claim: DTS default off causes split disbursement errors
quote: If the traveler fails to annotate the split amount (leaves the split amount blank) certifying officials will split the outstanding balance
fix: Split disbursement is mandatory. A blank amount makes the certifying official split the card balance.

claim: TLE not paid when trip outside CONUS
quote: TLE for either 7 or 21 days
fix: TLE is CONUS PCS. Outside CONUS the TLA path applies. Say TLA.

claim: Dispute open past 30 days warrants commander engagement
fix: Local practice.

claim: Default lodging Marine Corps official lodging at Marine installations per MARADMIN 234/26 effective 25 May 2026
quote: Marine Lodges and Inns of the Corps are official lodging facilities.

claim: Off-base lodging without certificate of non-availability needs certificate or rebook
quote: certificates of non-availability will only be issued if accommodations are not available.

claim: TDY destination set to the installation, not the city
quote: the TDY destination in DTS is listed as the installation (when applicable), not the associated city or town.

claim: Unsubmitted vouchers past 5 working days flagged weekly
quote: Travelers must submit a travel claim within five working days of completion of travel.
fix: Clock runs from completion of travel. Add the 30 and 90 day zero-dollar voucher triggers in paras 3.a and 3.d.

claim: Split disbursement default off, toggle ON before submission
quote: split disbursement is a required bill payment process
fix: Split is required and defaults to the card balance. It is not a profile toggle.

claim: No unsettled DTS debt at transfer
quote: Ensure any money owed from overpayments is repaid prior to detachment from the organization or separated from Active Duty

claim: Verify DTS profile within first 30 days
fix: Local practice.

claim: DTS profile locks from GTCC delinquency
fix: No archive source.
